Features

What you get

A complete AI-native desktop environment in one command.

Btrfs Agent Sandbox (Auto-Rollback)
Before your AI executes code or shell commands, Ash instantly takes a Btrfs CoW snapshot. If the agent breaks your OS, `ash sandbox rollback` instantly reverts the damage.
Anti-Slopsquatting Firewall
Wraps npm, pip, and cargo with a local proxy that checks requests against pre-seeded allowlists. Prevents hallucinations from installing malicious typosquatted dependencies.
NotebookLM Sync & Unified Context
Run `ash context` to run a semantic hybrid search via Qdrant and BM25 across your local codebase AND your synced Google NotebookLM knowledge bases instantly.
"Explain This Disaster" Mode
When an agent generates hundreds of lines of complex changes, press a hotkey to run `ash explain --diff`. Ash parses the git diff and generates a human-readable walkthrough of the logic.
Snapshot Branching ("Git for Sessions")
Fork entire OS workspace states into independent CoW subvolumes using `ash branch`. Test competing AI architecture approaches simultaneously on the same hardware.
Task-Specific Model Router
A local proxy routes Ollama requests on-the-fly. Small fast models for autocomplete, 32B models for architecture, and 7B models for refactoring — completely automatically.

Usage

Commands at your fingertips

Search by meaning. Filter by time. Ask questions. All from one launcher.

$lsfs-query 'database config files'
Semantic search — finds files by meaning, not keywords. Scored by cosine similarity to your query.
$lsfs-query 'files from last 3 days'
Time-based fallback — when semantic parsing can't handle relative time, fd takes over seamlessly.
⌘Super+Space → type → enter
Desktop launcher — search bar overlay. Results sorted by relevance. Opens in Kitty + Neovim.
$ash-doctor
40+ health checks — services, ports, permissions, GPU, disk space, index age. Exports to JSON.
$journalctl --user -u lsfs-daemon -f
Watch the indexer live. See files being embedded in real time as they're created or modified.
$curl ... | sudo bash
Re-run anytime. The installer is fully idempotent — detects existing state and resumes where it left off.
FAQ

Common questions

If yours isn't here, open an issue on GitHub.

No. The installer detects your existing system — desktop environment, package manager, GPU — and installs alongside. Only prerequisite is an internet connection for the initial download.
Zero telemetry by default. Everything runs locally — the embedding model, vector database, file indexer, and search. No data ever leaves your machine. Optional auto-update checks are the only network calls.
4GB RAM minimum, 8GB recommended. ~400MB for Qdrant + Ollama binaries, ~140MB for embedding model. Index size scales with your files (~2KB per file). Swap is auto-configured on low-memory systems.
Yes. Use --profile server to install Qdrant, Ollama, and the LSFS daemon without desktop components. Run lsfs-query from any terminal. The desktop profile adds Hyprland, Kitty, Wofi, and Super+Space bindings.
Spotlight searches filenames and metadata. Ash understands what your files mean — it reads content, generates vector embeddings, and returns results ranked by semantic relevance. It's also 100% offline, Linux-native, and indexes everything including config files and source code.
